evidence_boundary: Public documentary aggregates and official oversight findings only. No individual samples, coordinates, household records or health records.

sources.title: In 2023 the rate of violations in more than 5000 samples of food and drinking water is 12%
sources.evidence_note: Reports 624 non-compliances and a rounded 12% rate across a combined food-and-drinking-water sample set; not a drinking-water-only rate.

sources.title: Special Report on the Realisation of the Right to Water in Georgia
sources.evidence_note: Pages 33–34 describe planned drinking-water sample counts, publication/disclosure limitations and the need for consolidated, locally useful information.

sources.title: State Control and Monitoring Trends of Drinking Water Quality in Georgia
sources.evidence_note: Abstract describes a secondary analysis of 2020–2023 monitoring data and identifies microbiological violations as the main non-compliance type; full PDF tables were not re-extracted in this run.

disclosure_findings: The Public Defender report states that the NFA public monitoring spreadsheets include several food directions and water records from different source locations (including reservoirs, sources, yard taps and public institutions); although drinking water is separated, the published compilation does not readily expose a regional/municipal picture.
The Public Defender recommends a consolidated platform/database for drinking-water quality information and locally appropriate public communication rather than relying only on electronic publication.
The Public Defender report records field visits to 35 villages in 15 municipalities across five regions; these are fact-finding visits, not a representative national water-quality survey.
limitations: The NFA 12% and 624 figures cover a combined food-and-drinking-water sample set; the exact denominator and water-only numerator/denominator are not provided in the release.
The 520 (2023) and 850 (2024) values are planned drinking-water sample allocations, not observed completed sample counts.
The NFA 2023 XLSX payload was linked from the official portal but the current reader rejected the XLSX content type; no workbook bytes, hash or row-level contents were obtained.
The JECM article is a secondary analysis; its abstract was reviewed but the PDF tables were not re-extracted in this run.
No regional prevalence, national water-only non-compliance rate, causal health effect or legal compliance conclusion is estimated.
